claims.text: Google Public Sector says it is developing a proof-of-concept physical, robotic system that aims to support deep space missions and could assist astronauts during NASA missions.
claims.quote: Today, we are building on this innovation with the development of a proof-of-concept physical, robotic system that aims to support deep space missions and could assist astronauts during NASA missions.

claims.text: NASA's Human Research Program, the Johnson Space Center Robotics Team and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory collaborated with Google Public Sector to develop the robotic system.
claims.quote: NASA’s Human Research Program, Johnson Space Center Robotics Team, and the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) collaborated with Google Public Sector to develop a robotic system.

claims.text: In a proof-of-concept demonstration the system was tasked to locate and move a medical bag and achieved an initial 85% baseline success rate in early lab environments.
claims.quote: In a recent proof-of-concept technology demonstration, the robotic system was tasked with a complex "pick-and-place" maneuver to locate and move a medical bag. By implementing an "eye-to-hand" camera configuration for enhanced spatial awareness, the open-source Pi0 model—developed by Physical Intelligence on Google Cloud infrastructure— achieved an initial 85% baseline success rate in these early lab environments

claims.text: The system used the open-source Pi0 model developed by Physical Intelligence and run on Google Cloud infrastructure.
claims.quote: The system used the open-source Pi0 model, developed by AI software and research company Physical Intelligence and run on Google Cloud infrastructure.

claims.text: The Google team used Google Cloud G4 instances to fine-tune the 4-billion parameter Pi0 model in 2.5 hours.
claims.quote: the Google team harnessed Google Cloud G4 instances to rapidly train the underlying models, fine-tuning the 4-billion parameter Pi0 model in just 2.5 hours.

claims.text: Google DeepMind's MuJoCo simulator let the system practice movements in a virtual environment before touching real hardware.
claims.quote: Google DeepMind’s MuJoCo simulator was used, which is an advanced physics engine that allows the SI to practice complex movements in a highly accurate virtual environment before touching real hardware.

claims.text: The early lab demonstration took place at Johnson Space Center's iMETRO facility.
claims.quote: In an early laboratory demonstration at Johnson Space Center's iMETRO facility, the robot achieved an initial 85% success rate in locating and moving a medical bag.

claims.text: The demonstration used an eye-to-hand camera configuration for spatial awareness.
claims.quote: By implementing an "eye-to-hand" camera configuration for enhanced spatial awareness

claims.text: Jim Kelly, Vice President, Federal, Google Public Sector, wrote that the ultimate goal is a robotic system that executes tasks via simple voice instructions under the astronauts' direct supervision.
claims.quote: Looking ahead, the ultimate goal is to build a robotic system that can execute a variety of tasks via simple voice instructions, under the astronauts’ direct supervision and command.

claims.text: An astronaut on a Mars mission could face round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes, making real-time medical guidance nearly impossible.
claims.quote: An astronaut on a future deep space mission to Mars could face severe operational challenges—including round-trip communication latencies of up to 44 minutes, making real-time medical guidance for crew nearly impossible.

claims.text: The robot builds on the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant (CMO-DA), an automated clinical decision support system for real-time medical guidance.
claims.quote: Last year, Google Public Sector shared progress on the development of the Crew Medical Officer Digital Assistant (CMO-DA) - an automated Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) designed to assist astronauts with real-time medical guidance in remote and isolated environments.

claims.text: The work is framed around NASA's Artemis program, its Moon Base and the first crewed missions to Mars.
claims.quote: As NASA advances its Artemis program to send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions to explore more of the Moon, build a sustained human presence there with a Moon Base, and build on their foundation for the first crewed missions to Mars, crew safety and Earth-independent autonomy are paramount.

claims.text: The project is at the proof-of-concept stage and Google has not confirmed that a fully integrated, space-ready robot exists.
claims.quote: The project remains at the proof-of-concept stage, with early laboratory demonstrations conducted, but Google hasn't confirmed whether a fully integrated, space-ready robot exists.

claims.text: NASA's Johnson Space Center is in Houston.
claims.quote: The Dexterous Robotics Team at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston plays a key role in developing robotic hardware and software to support NASA’s bold vision for the future

claims.text: iMETRO at Johnson supports adapting terrestrial robots for human-supervised space work such as logistics, maintenance and science, with space vehicle and habitat mockups.
claims.quote: iMETRO is designed to support the adaptation of terrestrial robotic technologies for human-supervised space exploration applications such as logistics, maintenance, and scientific research. The facility comprises open-source software and simulation assets, as well as space vehicle and habitat mockups, a selection of “house robots,” and an outdoor rock yard.

claims.text: The robot is designed as a payload handler for cargo, logistics and equipment that can pivot to medical support, such as retrieving and preparing an ultrasound machine for an astronaut with severe back pain.
claims.quote: the robotic system is designed as a versatile "payload" handler capable of managing cargo, logistics, and equipment. When not needed for routine maintenance like organizing tools or securing compartments, it can pivot to medical support. For example, if an astronaut experiences severe back pain—a potential symptom of kidney stones—the robot could retrieve and prepare an ultrasound machine.

claims.text: Google announced the work in a blog post dated October 27th, 2026.
claims.quote:
Google Cloud and NASA: Testing robotic systems for deep space missions
October 27, 2026

claims.text: The team tested about 15 edge computing devices over two years and showed the fine-tuned models can run locally on compact, energy-efficient edge devices.
claims.quote: Crucially, they demonstrated that the fine-tuned models can then operate locally on compact, energy-efficient edge devices. Over the last two years, the team tested approximately 15 different edge computing devices to find ones that run efficiently on lightweight, low-power hardware required for future Mars missions.

claims.text: JPL is adapting satellite situational awareness tools, built to track objects in orbit, to help the robot navigate its 3D surroundings.
claims.quote: JPL is adapting satellite situational awareness intelligence tools—originally designed to track objects in orbit—to help the robotic system navigate and understand its 3D surroundings.

claims.text: Because vision-language-action models connect language to movement, astronauts could direct the robot with standard English text prompts.
claims.quote: Because vision-language-action (VLA) models connect language directly to physical movement, astronauts could direct the robotic system flexibly via standard English text prompts.

claims.text: The robot would leave the scan and treatment to the human crew medical officer and is not meant to replace human decision-making.
claims.quote: This ensures astronauts receive the physical assistance they might not be able to perform by themselves, without ever replacing human decision-making.

claims.text: Future tasks could include routine health monitoring such as capturing basic vitals or simple ultrasounds under a human crew medical officer.
claims.quote: For instance, the robot might be directed to assist with routine health monitoring—such as capturing basic vitals or simple ultrasounds—under the strict guidance of a human crew medical officer.

claims.text: A NASA spokesperson said work is ongoing with partners to assess these tools for potential future applications.
claims.quote: Work is ongoing by NASA and a variety of partners to analyze and assess these tools for potential future applications.

claims.text: A PickNik robot arm tested at iMETRO earlier opened a spacecraft hatch and moved cargo bags between the hatch and a bin.
claims.quote: In one case, a team from PickNik Inc. used iMETRO to test software enabling a robotic arm to recognize a spacecraft hatch, then turn the latch, grasp the handle, and open the door. The arm was then able to transfer cargo bags between the hatch and a bin.

cautions: 85% is an initial baseline in early lab environments on one locate-and-move-a-medical-bag task. Not a medical procedure and not tested in space.
Proof of concept only. No space-ready robot confirmed and no flight date.
Ultrasound, vitals and voice commands are goals and examples, not demonstrated abilities.
Pi0 was developed by Physical Intelligence and ran on Google Cloud. Google did not build Pi0.
The robot does not replace the crew medical officer.
44 minutes is the round-trip 'up to' figure for Mars.
No NASA person is tied to this project by name. People on screen are illustrative.
